reading.body:
Judy Chu's AI record is mostly cosponsorship: eleven of thirteen dated events are bills she signed onto, and the two data center bills among them are the only ones that touch compute directly.

The bills split into two clusters. One governs what AI does to people: biometric surveillance, advertising disclosure, civil rights, workplace automation, price gouging. The other governs what AI does to land and power: a ban on data centers on federal lands and a bill on data center energy costs. The second cluster is small but it is the part that connects to the physical buildout, and it appears in the record later than most of the rights bills.

The single contribution, $1,000 from Amazon's PAC in September 2025, is the only money in the record. One contribution from one committee is not a pattern, and the data does not say what it was for or what followed it.

What the record does not cover matters as much as what it does. It holds no committee votes, no amendments, no floor statements, and no spending beyond that one filing. Cosponsorship is a low-cost act, so the volume of bills here shows interest, not influence. The dates are latest-status dates for bills, not the dates Chu acted, so the sequence should not be read as a chronology of her decisions.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Judy Chu: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 13 events.
